title: Lead Carpenter Day
short_answer: What "owning the room" means before the first screw: packet, crew brief, stage plan, QC, Job Check, and the stops that protect margin.
summary: A lead makes sure the crew does the right work, in the right order, to the right standard, and that Monday and the office know the truth.
plain_words: A lead is not the fastest hanger. A lead is the person who makes sure the crew does the right work, in the right order, to the right standard, and that Monday and the office know the truth. Full detail in this manual is written for you — use Plain when you teach.
when_to_use: Every day you are lead on a GVC job
Opening and closing a production day
Before advancing Job Check stages or calling a stage done
prerequisites: Job Start packet accepted and read

steps.title: Open the packet
steps.body: Open the Job Start / handoff packet — exclusions, open questions, lock box, board count, window/ceiling notes. Do not invent missing facts.

steps.title: Walk the area
steps.body: Walk the area before the crew dumps material. Photo conditions you will be blamed for later.

steps.title: Crew brief
steps.body: Brief the crew in five minutes: today's stage, what "done" looks like, what is out of scope, who to call.

steps.title: Stage the work
steps.body: Stock to the work, not the door. Split the crew so hangers are not waiting on layout and finishers are not standing in scrap.

steps.title: Mid-day QC
steps.body: Short walk; catch butt-joint layout sins and dirty boxes before mud.

steps.title: Job Check
steps.body: Update Job Check when a stage is actually done — not when you hope it is done.

steps.title: CO / stop events
steps.body: Photo, write, call. Standing-by is a documentation event.

steps.title: End of day
steps.body: Photos to the job Pictures habit, leftover material staged, tomorrow's first hour set, Action Requests cleared.

warnings.title: Never advance Job Check for the GC
warnings.body: Never advance Job Check to make a GC happy if the stage is not true. Monday truth is the office SoT.

warnings.title: Open questions from handoff
warnings.body: If open questions from the handoff are unanswered, that is Ops/Sales work — not a field improvisation contest.

experts.tag: Full detail · splitting a crew without rework
experts.summary: Batch by operation — layout first, then batch — scales to the whole day. One person chasing punch while three hang the next floor is fine; three people each "finishing their own room" to different standards is how touch-up explodes. Teach with Plain mode; decide with Full detail. Never advance Job Check to make a GC happy if the stage is not true. If open questions from the handoff are unanswered, that is Ops/Sales work — not a field improvisation contest.

quality_checks.prompt: Handoff packet opened; exclusions and open questions reviewed
Five-minute crew brief: stage, done, out-of-scope, who to call
Mid-day QC walk before mud closes layout sins
Job Check updated only when stage is actually true

common_mistakes.title: Fastest hanger ≠ lead
common_mistakes.wrong: Outproduce the crew without briefing or QC
common_mistakes.right: Own order, standard, and Monday truth

common_mistakes.title: Hope-based Job Check
common_mistakes.wrong: Flip Hanging to done before scrape is ready
common_mistakes.right: Save when the stage is actually complete

common_mistakes.title: Field invention on open questions
common_mistakes.wrong: Build through an unanswered handoff blocker
common_mistakes.right: Send back to Ops/Sales until answered
